label: Romance poem ending, line 2B
summary: Writes one closing line of a rhyming romance poem, picked at random from three.
details: The three lines end in 'tree', 'free' and 'tea'. Going by its name, it belongs to the closing lines of a romance poem; the input does not say where exactly. The second option mentions the poem's subject (the character saved in the variable poem_subject) with the matching 'her' or 'him'. Runs on a character.

label: Romance poem ending, line 3A
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming romance poem about the subject's smile.
details: All three options give the same text (the second and third just point to the first): the mere thought of the subject's smile brings one to my face. The subject is the character saved in the variable poem_subject; the text uses 'her' or 'his'. Going by its name, it is the first line of a pair that the 3B entry completes.

label: Romance poem ending, line 3B
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming romance poem that rhymes with 'face', picked at random from three.
details: The three lines end in 'place', 'pace' and 'trace'. They rhyme with the line of the 3A entry, which ends in 'face'. Going by its name, it is the second line of that pair.

label: Strife poem ending, line 1A
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming strife poem about the subject's subjects having to be grateful.
details: All three options give the same text (the second and third just point to the first): the subject's subjects prove grateful, for if they are not. The subject is the character saved in the variable poem_subject; the text uses their 'her' or 'his', capitalised because it opens the line. Going by its name, it is the first line of a pair that the 1B entry completes.

label: Strife poem ending, line 1B
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming strife poem that rhymes with 'not', picked at random from three.
details: The lines end in 'brought', 'wrought' and 'fought'; the 1A entry ends in 'not'. The first mentions the poem's subject (the character in the variable poem_subject) with 'her' or 'his'. Going by its name, it is the second line of the pair started by the 1A entry.

label: Strife poem ending, line 2A
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming strife poem: all shall tremble as the subject takes field.
details: All three options give the same text (the second and third just point to the first): then all shall tremble as the subject takes field. 'She' or 'he' is chosen from the gender of the character saved in the variable poem_subject. Going by its name, it is the first line of a pair that the 2B entry completes.

label: Strife poem ending, line 2B
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming strife poem that rhymes with 'field', picked at random from three.
details: The lines end in 'shield', 'wield' and 'heal'; the 2A entry ends in 'field'. The third starts with the poem's subject's 'her' or 'his' (capitalised; the subject is the character in the variable poem_subject).

label: Strife poem ending, line 3A
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming strife poem telling nobody to challenge the subject's bold intent.
details: All three options give the same text (the second and third just point to the first): so let none challenge the subject's bold intent. The subject is the character saved in the variable poem_subject; the text uses their 'her' or 'his'. Going by its name, it is the first line of a pair that the 3B entry completes.

label: Strife poem ending, line 3B
summary: Writes a closing line of a rhyming strife poem that rhymes with 'intent', picked at random from three.
details: The lines end in 'went', 'sent' and 'rent'. They are threats against anyone who challenges the poem's subject.

label: Poem title
summary: Builds the title of a generated poem from a random pattern.
details: The game lists 25 patterns, five each for romance, mourning, legacy, strife and incompetence; the input shows the first 12 names and four texts. A pattern is a sentence frame filled with other random word lists, for example a season and an emotion ('Summer of Love') or 'My' plus an adjective and an emotion. Runs on a character.

label: Poem title activity
summary: Gives a random sad activity for a poem title.
details: The options are Weeping Tears, Silent Longing, Fitful Slumber and Harsh Sobbing. Poem titles use it in patterns like 'Activity in Season'.

label: Poem title adjective
summary: Gives a random romantic adjective for a poem title.
details: The options are Romantic, Amorous, Intimate and Passionate. Poem titles use it in patterns like 'My Adjective Emotion'.

label: Poem title emotion
summary: Gives a random emotion noun for a poem title, such as Love, Sorrow or Wrath.
details: There are twelve options: four loving (Love, Passion, Tenderness, Doting), four sad (Sadness, Sorrow, Regret, Mourning) and four angry (Rage, Anger, Bloodlust, Wrath). The input shows the texts of the first four only; the rest follow from the entry names.

label: Poem title emotion, adjective
summary: Gives the adjective form of a random emotion for a poem title.
details: It has the same twelve emotions as the emotion list, with _adj entries. The input shows no text for them, so the exact wording is not known here.

label: Poem title intensity
summary: Gives a random adverb of intensity for a poem title.
details: The options are Gently, Firmly, Copiously and Strenuously.

label: Poem title place
summary: Gives a random figurative place for a poem title: Heart, Head, Dreams or Chest.
details: Poem titles use it in patterns like 'A Simple Season in My Place'.

label: Poem title place, adjective
summary: Gives the adjective form of a random figurative place for a poem title.
details: It has the same four places as the place list (heart, head, dreams, chest), with _adj entries. The input shows no text for them, so the exact wording is not known here.

label: Poem title noun
summary: Gives a random noun for a poem title, from fond ones (Memory, Legacy) to quarrelsome and insulting ones.
details: There are 14 options. The input shows 12 names: Memory, Legacy, Memoriam, Heritage, Strife, Penury, Conflict, Quarrel and some rude words (arse, carbuncle, fool, idiot); the last two names are villain and spawn. Texts are shown only for the first four.

label: Poem title mood scenery
summary: Gives a random gloomy piece of scenery for a poem title, such as Windswept Woods.
details: The options are Windswept Woods, Rainy Nights, Still Mornings and Lonely Graves.

label: Poem title scenery, adjective
summary: Gives the adjective form of a random piece of gloomy scenery for a poem title.
details: It has the same four sceneries as the mood scenery list, with _adj entries. The input shows no text for them, so the exact wording is not known here.

label: Poem title season
summary: Gives a random season for a poem title: spring, summer, autumn or winter.
details: The words are lowercase; poem titles capitalise them with the |U formatting where needed.

label: Poem title season, adjective
summary: Gives a random adjective that describes a season for a poem title.
details: The options are fresh (spring), sweltering (summer), humid (autumn) and cold (winter).

label: Poem title weapon
summary: Gives a random weapon name for a poem title: Sword, Spear, Axe, Lance or Mace.
details: The input shows the texts of the first four only; Mace follows from its entry name. Poem titles use the weapon word as part of a title; the input does not show which patterns.

label: Poem title weapon, adjective
summary: Gives the adjective form of a random weapon word for a poem title.
details: It has the same five weapons as the weapon list (sword, spear, axe, lance, mace), with _adj entries. The input shows no text for them, so the exact wording is not known here.

label: Poem title verb
summary: Gives a random verb in -ing form for a poem title, mostly unflattering ones such as Drooling or Failing.
details: There are seven options: Drooling, Defecating, Failing, Collapsing, Meandering, Slacking and Cumbergrounding. The input shows the texts of the first four only.

label: Friendly gesture
summary: Writes a friendly gesture at random: bowing deeply to the character, or clasping their hands.
details: The two texts are 'bows deeply to' followed by the character's first name, and 'clasps' followed by the possessive of the first name and 'hands'. Both use forms named 'OrMe'; going by that name, they may say 'me' or 'my' in some situation (perhaps when the character is the speaker), but the input does not say when.

label: Accessory
summary: Gives the name of a random clothing accessory, such as an earring, bow or bracelet.
details: There are 14 options. The input shows 12 names (earring, bow, bracelet, snood, garter, gauntlet, cap, nose ring, sash, shawl, scarf, sock) and two more, fan and muff. Texts are shown for the first four only.

label: Activity reason
summary: Describes what the character is busy with, as a short phrase.
details: The entry names all start with 'unavailable', so the phrases look meant to explain why the character is unavailable. Examples: 'participating in' the character's current activity, 'paying homage to your liege', 'bowing before your liege', 'meditating'. Nine options in all, named pay homage, pledge loyalty, meditation, local shrine, petition liege, petition head of faith, hold court and tour stop. Not random: the input does not show how the entry is chosen.

label: Activity special score name
summary: Gives the name of an activity's special progress score, such as Piousness Achieved or Carousing.
details: The four options are Piousness Achieved and Worldliness Achieved (pilgrimage), Studiousness (adult education) and Carousing (camp party). Runs on an activity. Not random.

label: Activity special score help
summary: Gives the help text that explains an activity's special progress score.
details: For a pilgrimage it says how Pious or Worldly the pilgrimage has turned out so far, and that a higher score can give better activity rewards. The camp party text says the same about Carousing. Each text starts with two line breaks, so it looks meant to be appended to other text. Runs on an activity. Not random.

label: Bishop-level title
summary: Gives the title of a religious office-holder for the character's faith, such as a chaplain or a head of faith.
details: There are 129 entries. They cover the faith head's name (also in an 'Anti' form, and the Ecumenical Patriarch or Matriarch) and the titles of court chaplains and holders of church titles in many faiths, with male and female forms and county, duchy, kingdom or empire levels. Some entries appear twice in the documented list. Not random.

label: Bishop-level title, possessive
summary: Gives the possessive form (with 's) of the religious office title from the bishop-title list.
details: It follows the bishop-title list with _possessive added to each name, but is shorter: 119 entries against 129. A few entries of the original (for example the Korean and Vietnamese Buddhist ones) have no possessive entry. Example: the ecumenical patriarch entry is the patriarch title plus 's. Not random.

label: Church count title
summary: Gives the title of a church-ruled county's holder, such as Cardinal or Prince-Archbishop.
details: Five options, by gender and by role (cardinal, archbishop holder, default). The texts shown are Cardinal, Princess-Archbishop, Prince-Archbishop and Princess-Bishop; the text of the default male form is not shown. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Church duke title
summary: Gives the title of a church-ruled duchy's holder, such as Cardinal, Catholicos or a prince-archbishop title.
details: There are 15 entries: faith head titles for Coptic and Apostolic churches, Cardinal, archbishop-holder titles, some orthodox and catholic chaplain titles and the default male and female duke titles. Not random.

label: Band name animal
summary: Gives a random animal or creature name, in the plural, for naming an adventurer band.
details: There are 94 options, from bulls, wolves and eagles to dragons, unicorns, and Asian creatures such as tengus, nagas and onis. The texts are capitalised plurals (Bulls, Bears, Wolves).

label: Band name group
summary: Gives a random group word for an adventurer band's name, such as Brothers, Rangers or Warband.
details: There are 95 options, from military ones (Legion, Archers, Pikemen) to religious (Monks, Pilgrims, Inquisitors) and outlaw ones (Bandits, Exiles).

label: Band name adjective
summary: Gives a random adjective that opens an adventurer band's name, such as Fiery, Iron or Golden.
details: There are 94 options: metals and colours, stern or noble words, weather and seasons. Texts are capitalised.

label: Band name devout group
summary: Gives a random group word for an adventurer band's name, from a shorter list that fits a devout band.
details: It has 74 options, most of them also in the general group list (Cohort, Pilgrims, Monks, Prophets). It leaves out outlaw words such as Bandits, Outlaws and Rogues and adds Anointed. The name 'reverent' suggests it is used for religious bands; the input does not say.

label: Band name object
summary: Gives a random object or place word that ends an adventurer band's name, such as Cape, Shield or Fortress.
details: There are 337 options: clothes, armour, buildings, weapons, tools, instruments and Asian items. A few look out of place, such as 'bollocks' and 'privy'.

label: Band name sword group
summary: Gives a random group word for an adventurer band's name, from a list of 40 words.
details: The words are Bastards, Cohort, Vanguard, Band, Guard, Seekers, Riders, Pilgrims, Sages, Kings and similar. Going by its name, it is meant for bands named after a sword and used together with the weapon list; the input does not say.

label: Band name weapon
summary: Gives a random weapon word for an adventurer band's name, such as Lance, Halberd or Blade.
details: There are 30 options, from European arms (Mace, Flail, Pike, Misericorde) to Asian ones (Jian, Dao, Katana, Kris, Shuriken). Texts are capitalised.

label: Camp purpose name
summary: Gives the name of an adventurer camp's purpose, such as wanderers, mercenaries or scholars.
details: Each of the six options simply shows the name of the matching camp-purpose law: wanderers, mercenaries, scholars, explorers, brigands and legitimists. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Afterlife fate
summary: Describes where the character's soul goes after death, in a short phrase.
details: Three options: reincarnated in a new form, suffering in the faith's negative afterlife for their sins, or resting peacefully in the faith's positive afterlife. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Ancestor first name
summary: Gives the first name of a legend's ancestor: either the ancestor flag's name or the ancestor character's first name.
details: The first option is the ancestor flag's name (capitalised); the second is the first name of the character saved as the legend's ancestor property. The input does not show when each is used. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor first name, plain
summary: Gives the same as the ancestor first name, but the character's first name has no hover tooltip.
details: The first option is the capitalised ancestor flag name, as in the other entry; the second uses the first-name form without a tooltip. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor first name, possessive
summary: Gives the possessive of a legend's ancestor: the flag name with 's, or the ancestor's first name.
details: The first option is the capitalised ancestor flag name plus 's. The second option, for a named ancestor, shows the first name without an 's added in the input text, which looks odd for a possessive. The input does not show when each is used. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor possessive, plain
summary: Gives the possessive first name of a legend's ancestor, without a hover link.
details: The first option is the capitalised flag name plus 's. The second uses the first name without a tooltip, shown in the input without an added 's. The input does not show when each is used. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor name
summary: Gives the name of a legend's ancestor: either the ancestor flag's name or the ancestor character's name.
details: The first option is the capitalised ancestor flag name; the second is the name of the character saved as the legend's ancestor property. The input does not show when each is used. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor name, plain
summary: Gives the name of a legend's ancestor without a hover link.
details: Like the ancestor name, but the character's name has no tooltip; the first option is still the capitalised ancestor flag name. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor name, possessive
summary: Gives the possessive of a legend's ancestor: the flag name with 's, or the ancestor character's possessive name.
details: The first option is the capitalised flag name plus 's; the second uses the character's possessive name form. The input does not show when each is used. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Ancestor possessive, plain
summary: Gives the possessive name of a legend's ancestor without a hover link.
details: Like the possessive ancestor name, but the character's name has no tooltip; the first option is the capitalised flag name plus 's. Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Animal adjective
summary: Gives a random adjective for a hunted animal, such as flighty, majestic or sly.
details: There are 14 options: 12 in the input (flighty, majestic, powerful, sly, quick, devious, swift, leaping, prancing, despised, loathsome, cunning) plus fabled and mystical. It works in any scope.

label: Captive animal adjective
summary: Gives a random adjective for a captive animal: majestic, powerful, ferocious or deadly.
details: A shorter list than the general animal adjective, with fierce words that fit a caged beast. It works in any scope.

label: Animal article
summary: Gives 'an' or 'a', the article that fits the animal's name.
details: Not random: the input does not show how the entry is chosen. Going by its name, it depends on the animal's name. Its scope is 'all', so it works anywhere.

label: Animal charge verb
summary: Gives a random verb for how a hunted animal charges: bound, charge, lope or hurtle.
details: It works in any scope.

label: Animal charge verb (kill)
summary: Gives a random verb for how an animal charges in a hunt's kill scene: bound, charge, lope or hurtle.
details: It has the same four options as the general charge verb, but runs on an activity. The name suggests it is used when the hunt ends in a kill.

label: Animal young
summary: Gives a random word for a young animal: calf, fawn, pup, kitten, leveret, piglet or cub.
details: The last option is a fallback word for animals with no special name. It works in any scope.

label: Animal colour
summary: Gives a random fur colour or pattern word, such as brown, golden or spotted.
details: There are 18 options, including colours (brown, black, white, orange), shades (dark, bright, sandy) and patterns (spotted, speckled). It works in any scope.

label: Animal dangerous part
summary: Gives a random dangerous body part of an animal: antlers, horns, fangs, claws, tusks or teeth.
details: It works in any scope.

label: Animal dangerous part (kill)
summary: Gives a random dangerous body part of an animal, for the kill scene: antlers, horns, fangs, claws, tusks or teeth.
details: Same six options as the general version. The name suggests it is used when the hunt ends in a kill.

label: Animal feature
summary: Gives a random striking feature of an animal, such as branching antlers or a shaggy coat.
details: There are 13 options (antlers, horns, coat, spots, stripes, tusks, tail, mane, legs, neck, bill, plumage, long legs). The texts shown pair a feature with an adjective, for example 'coiled horns'. It works in any scope.

label: Animal feature (kill)
summary: Gives a random striking feature of an animal for the kill scene, such as snarling fangs.
details: Twelve options. Compared with the general feature list it adds fangs and claws and drops spots, stripes and mane. The name suggests it is used when the hunt ends in a kill.

label: Female animal word
summary: Gives a random word for a female animal, such as doe, vixen, cow or mare.
details: There are 12 options. The last is a fallback for animals with no special word. It works in any scope.

label: Animal group word
summary: Gives a random collective word for a group of animals, such as herd, pack, pride or flock.
details: There are 18 options, including unusual ones (sloth, sounder, skulk, husk, mustering, sedge). The last is plain 'group'. It works in any scope.

label: Animal group word, plural
summary: Gives the plural of a random group word, such as herds, packs or prides.
details: It mirrors the group list, 18 options with _plural. It works in any scope.

label: Male animal word
summary: Gives a random word for a male animal, such as buck, dog, bull or stallion.
details: The options also include the animal types boar, lion, tiger and leopard, and a fallback. Note that the entry called stag shows the word 'buck'. It works in any scope.

label: Animal sighting text
summary: Writes a short hunting sighting message for a title, such as animals sighted in or terrorizing the title's name.
details: Four variants: standard (animals sighted in the title), dangerous (terrorizing), legendary (a legendary colour and animal rumored in) and falconry (sighted in). The animal words come from other custom texts called on the title, and the title's name is used without its rank. Runs on a title. Not random.

label: Animal sound
summary: Gives a random animal sound, such as bark, growl, roar or honk.
details: There are 13 options (bark, snort, growl, bellow, roar, scream, laugh, howl, squeal, squeak, quack, honk, call). It works in any scope.

label: Animal sound, -ing form (kill)
summary: Gives a random animal sound in -ing form, such as barking or growling, for the kill scene.
details: Ten options, matching the first ten sounds (up to squeak). The name suggests it is used when the hunt ends in a kill.

label: Animal strike
summary: Gives a random way an animal strikes: kick, buck, bite, swipe or strike.
details: It works in any scope.

label: Animal strike, -ing form (kill)
summary: Gives a random way an animal strikes in -ing form: kicking, bucking, biting, swiping or striking.
details: Matches the strike list. The name suggests it is used when the hunt ends in a kill.

label: Animal track
summary: Gives the kind of footprint an animal leaves: hoof, trotter or paw.
details: Not random: the input does not show how the entry is chosen; going by its name, it depends on the animal. It works in any scope.

label: Animal type
summary: Gives the name of the hunted animal, such as saiga, wolf, bear, unicorn or pheasant.
details: There are 37 options: deer and antelope, bison, fox and hare, predators, birds and fantasy animals (unicorn, dragon). Not random: the input does not show how the entry is chosen. Note that the entry called buck shows the word 'stag'. It works in any scope.

label: Captive animal type
summary: Gives the name of a captive animal: lion, tiger, leopard, bear, lynx, hyena or wolf.
details: A short list of dangerous animals. Not random. It works in any scope.

label: Gamebird type
summary: Gives the name of a gamebird: pheasant, bustard, grouse or quail.
details: Not random. It works in any scope.

label: Animal type (kill)
summary: Gives the name of the animal, for the kill scene of a hunt.
details: It has 22 options, the general animal list without the unicorn, dragon and birds. Not random. It works in any scope.

label: Mismanaged animal type
summary: Gives the name of a deer or antelope: saiga, antelope, reindeer, stag, elk, hart, gazelle or roe.
details: It has the same eight options as the tame animal list. The name suggests it is used for a herd that was badly looked after; the input does not say. Not random.

label: Tame animal type
summary: Gives the name of a deer or antelope: saiga, antelope, reindeer, stag, elk, hart, gazelle or roe.
details: Same eight options as the mismanaged list. Going by its name, it is used for tame animals; the input does not say more. Not random. It works in any scope.

label: Waterfowl type
summary: Gives the name of a waterbird: swan, goose or duck.
details: Not random. It works in any scope.

label: Young animal word
summary: Gives a random word for a young animal: brocket, squeaker or juvenile.
details: Juvenile is the fallback. Runs on an activity.

label: Antiquarian or armorer
summary: Gives the name of the position, Armorer for a camp officer or Antiquarian for a court position.
details: Runs on a character. Not random; the input does not show how the entry is chosen.

label: Fitting name for the divine
summary: Gives a fitting word for the divine, for a motto: God, the Perfected Ones, the Divine or the Gods.
details: A fifth entry is a custom one. Runs on a character. Not random; the entry presumably fits the character's faith, but the input does not show the rule.

label: Foreign emissary aptitude
summary: Shows the aptitude (how suited the character is) as a percentage for the foreign emissary position, or a range when it is missing.
details: The first option shows the value of the script value foreign_emissary_aptitude_tooltip as a whole percentage. The second shows the range 2-10 in positive colour, 'based on aptitude'. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Yeke jarquchi aptitude
summary: Shows the aptitude (how suited the character is) as a percentage for the Yeke Jarquchi position, or a range when it is missing.
details: The first option shows the value of the script value yeke_jarquchi_aptitude_tooltip as a whole percentage. The second shows the range 2-10 in positive colour, 'based on aptitude'. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Age and gender phrase
summary: Describes the character with an article, age and gender, such as 'a young woman' or 'an elderly man'.
details: Five options. The texts shown are 'an elderly', 'a middle-aged', 'a' and 'a young' followed by the word for woman or man, which follows the character's gender; the fifth, named a_young_girl_boy, has no text in the input (its name suggests 'a young girl or boy'). Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Artifact decay
summary: Gives a random phrase for how an artifact has worn, such as 'its surface full of cracks'.
details: Six options. The texts shown are 'scratched and punctured', 'sharp ends dull', 'bindings and fabric torn' and 'surface full of cracks'; the other two are named fracture and worn. Runs on an artifact.

label: Aspect concept
summary: Gives the game-concept link for one of four aspects: creation, serenity, destruction or trickery.
details: Each option is a link to the matching concept, such as aspect of creation. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Aspect noun
summary: Gives the plain word for one of four aspects: creation, serenity, destruction or trickery.
details: Unlike the aspect concept, it is plain text without a link. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Aunt or uncle
summary: Gives 'aunt' or 'uncle'.
details: Runs on a character. Not random; the input does not show how the entry is chosen, but the words imply it follows the character's gender.

label: Auntie or uncle
summary: Gives 'auntie' or 'uncle'.
details: The same as the aunt or uncle word, but the female form is the friendlier 'auntie'. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Bad weather
summary: Gives a random bad-weather word, such as blizzard, sandstorm, storm, thunderstorm, downpour or gale.
details: Runs on a province.

label: Bastard explanation
summary: Explains that the character is a bastard, and for a highborn one that they are not a legitimate member of their house.
details: Two options: the highborn text names the character's house; the lowborn text only says they are a bastard. The sentence starts with 'You are' when the character is the local player, otherwise a third-person form. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Beauty comparison
summary: Gives a comparison for a beautiful character, such as 'an angel', 'a valkyrie' or 'Aphrodite herself'.
details: Eight options: angel, valkyrie, Aphrodite, Adonis, Rati, Kamadeva, Lilith and a default. Going by the names, the figure is chosen to fit the character's faith or gender, but the input does not show the rule. Runs on a character. Not random.

label: Praise for an empire
summary: Gives a flattering name for an empire, such as 'Glorious Rome' or 'Endless Mongolia'.
details: Seven options: Rome, Mongolia, Outremer, Slavia, Great Armenia, India and a generic one. Runs on a character. Not random; the input does not show how the empire is picked.

label: Bird insult
summary: Gives a random insult comparing someone to something, such as 'round as an egg' or 'as graceful as a goose'.
details: Nine options, for example 'shaped like a brick' and 'heavy like a stone'; the others are named barely a fledgeling, as thick as you, wobbly like a duck, as fast as a mountain and as bright as a rain cloud. Runs on a character.

label: Bird name
summary: Gives a random name, such as Rose, Ill-Fated, Ankle-Biter or 'petal'.
details: Nine options: swan names (Ill-Fated, Rose, Ankle-Biter), pet names (petal, songbird, beauty, spring blossom) and food names (biscuit, almond). Texts are shown for the first four; the rest follow from the entry names. Runs on a character.

label: Legend birth
summary: Describes the birth of a legendary figure: 'born to a virgin mother' or 'born under auspicious stars'.
details: Runs on a legend. Not random.

label: Birth omen
summary: Gives a random sign seen at a birth: a caul, an extra finger or a strange birthmark.
details: Runs on a character.

label: Bride or groom
summary: Gives 'bride' or 'groom'.
details: Runs on a character. Not random; the input does not show how the entry is chosen, but the words imply it follows the character's gender.

label: Building or dwelling
summary: Gives 'dwelling' or 'building'.
details: The entries are named is_dwelling and is_building; the input does not say when each applies. Runs on a character. Not random.
